doc.md:
Describes sorting criteria for a [`SortListModel`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SortListModel).

Its primary user is [`SortListModel`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SortListModel)

The model will use a sorter to determine the order in which
its items should appear by calling [`Sorter.compare()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Sorter#method:compare)
for pairs of items.

Sorters may change their sorting behavior through their lifetime.
In that case, they will emit the [`Sorter::changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Sorter#event:changed) signal
to notify that the sort order is no longer valid and should be updated
by calling gtk_sorter_compare() again.

GTK provides various pre-made sorter implementations for common sorting
operations. [`ColumnView`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColumnView) has built-in support for sorting lists
via the [`ColumnViewColumn:sorter`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColumnViewColumn#property:sorter) property, where the user can
change the sorting by clicking on list headers.

Of course, in particular for large lists, it is also possible to subclass
`GtkSorter` and provide one's own sorter.

changed.brief: Notifies all users of the sorter that it has changed.
changed.md:
Notifies all users of the sorter that it has changed.

This emits the [`Sorter::changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Sorter#event:changed) signal. Users
of the sorter should then update the sort order via
[`Sorter.compare()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Sorter#method:compare).

Depending on the `change` parameter, it may be possible to
update the sort order without a full resorting. Refer to
the [`SorterChange`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SorterChange) documentation for details.

This function is intended for implementers of `GtkSorter`
subclasses and should not be called from other functions.

compare.brief: Compares two given items according to the sort order implemented by the sorter.
compare.md:
Compares two given items according to the sort order implemented
by the sorter.

Sorters implement a partial order:

* It is reflexive, ie a = a
* It is antisymmetric, ie if a < b and b < a, then a = b
* It is transitive, ie given any 3 items with a ≤ b and b ≤ c,
  then a ≤ c

The sorter may signal it conforms to additional constraints
via the return value of [`Sorter.get_order()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Sorter#method:get_order).

get_order.brief: Gets the order that `self` conforms to.
get_order.md:
Gets the order that `self` conforms to.

See [`SorterOrder`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SorterOrder) for details
of the possible return values.

This function is intended to allow optimizations.

changed.md:
Emitted whenever the sorter changed.

Users of the sorter should then update the sort order
again via gtk_sorter_compare().

[`SortListModel`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SortListModel) handles this signal automatically.

Depending on the `change` parameter, it may be possible to update
the sort order without a full resorting. Refer to the
[`SorterChange`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SorterChange) documentation for details.
